pages.text: Concrete starts with $(item)limesand$(): crush Create's $(item)limestone$() with crushing wheels.$(br2)$(l)In a mixer$()$(br)Every step runs in a Create mechanical mixer over a basin, no heat needed:$(li)$(item)clay ball + limesand$() gives $(item)4 cement$(),

$(li)$(item)sand + cement + gravel$() gives $(item)16 concrete mixture$() (with $(item)slag$() instead of sand: $(item)32$()),$(li)$(item)concrete mixture + 250 mB water$() gives $(item)1000 mB liquid concrete$().

$(l)In a chemical vat$()$(br)With an industrial mixer, any chemical vat turns $(item)sand + gravel + limesand + 250 mB water$() straight into liquid concrete. JEI lists $(item)32000 mB$() for one batch, far more than the mixer route.
Cement is also a block of its own that falls like sand. Slag, from crushing the slag blocks of your steel line, doubles every batch of mixture.

Liquid concrete moves through pipes like any fluid and fills buckets. Poured into the world, it $(item)hardens into concrete blocks$() after a short random delay. The next pages show the three ways to use it: plain blocks, rebar, and the concrete hose.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
